case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated 20.03.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2359 of 2006)
full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J. This Civil Appeal No. 220 of 2016 is directed against the judgment and decree dated 20.03.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2359 of 2006 making the rule absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 26.04.2006 of the 2nd Court of Additional District Judge, Brahmanharia in Title Appeal No. 118 of 1997 and restoring the judgment and decree dated 30.10.1997 of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Brahmanbaria in Title Suit No. 10 of 1994.

<u>Background of the case</u>

<u>2. Plaintiff Gangacharan Debnath and others filed Title Suit No. 10 of 1994 before the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Brahmanbaria (the trial Court) for declaration of their title to the property measuring an area of 15 decimals of homestead property of C.S Plot No. 1069, S.A Plot No. 1350 under Mouza, Police Station and District-Brahmanbaria (previously Tripura District) as described in the 2nu schedule of the plaint (hereinafter referred to as the suit property) and 23 decimals of pond of C.S Plot No. 1068, S.A Plot No. 1349 under Mouza, Police Station and District-Brahmanbaria (previously Tripura District) as described in the 3rd schedule of the plaint(hereinafter referred to as the suit pond) stating, inter alia, that the suit property and suit pond along with some other lands as described in the 1st schedule of the plaint originally belonged to Kunja Mohan Debnath (Kunja), Piyare Mohan Debnath (Piyare), Raj Mohan Nath (Raj) and Sarupa Sundari Nath (Sarupa). Their names were duly recorded in C.S khatian Nos. 632, 633 and 634 of C.S. Plot Nos. 1064, 1069, 1060, 1068 and 1063 for 83 decimals of land. Kunja died leaving behind wife Muktakeshi Nath (Muktakeshi) and daughter Suchitra Debi (Suchitra), Muktakeshi filed Title Suit No. 241 of 1933 against the father of the defendant Nos. 1-3 i,e. Banamali Debnath (Banamali), son of Piyare, Raj and others for partition of the 1st schedule property along with other properties. Mahananda Debnath (Mahananda), father of the plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 were added as defendant No. 4 in the said suit. The said suit being Title Suit No. 241 of 1933 was decreed on compromise. According to Solenama and final decree the plaintiff of partition suit Muktakeshi got 15 decimals of homestead land from C.S. Plot No. 1069, 05 decimals from C.S Plot No. 1064, 01 decimal from C.S. Plot No. 1062 and 10 /9 decimals i.e. 4/9 share from C.S. Plot No. 1068 out of 23 decimals. Banamali, father of the defendant Nos. 1-3 got 13 decimals of lands in some other plots and Chapala got 05 decimals. Muktakeshi by registered deed date 07.05.1942 sold the suit property and 5 ¾ decimals of the pond out of the suit pond in favour of Sanatan Debnath (Sanatan) and delivered possession to Sanatan. Suchitra got 05 decimals of land of C.S. Plot No. 1064 after the death of her mother. Banamali, father of the defendant Nos. 1-3 fraudulently created a deed of purchase from Suchitra, Thereafter, Banamali filed a pre-emption case against Sanatan in the 2nd Court of Munsif, Brahmanbaria in the year 1945. But that suit was dismissed on contest. Thereafter, Banamali filed another suit being Title Suit No. 20 of 1947 and the said suit was also dismissed on contest. Sanatan had been in exclusive possession of the suit property and 5 ¾ decimals share in the suit pond for more than 12(twelve) years. Thereafter, in 1952, he sold the suit property and his share to the suit pond in favour of Gangacharan Debnath (Gangacharan) plaintiff No. 1 and Mahananda, father of the plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 verbally on receipt of part consideration money. But Gangacharan and Mahananada could not pay the entire price for which the document of sale could not be registered. As they were relatives, Gangacharan and Mahananda did not deem it necessary for registration of a sale deed in their favour from Sanatan. The plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit property by erecting homestead thereon and enjoying their share of the suit pond with other co-sharers. Banamali once set fire to the house of the plaintiffs for which all the documents of the plaintiffs were burnt into ashes. The plaintiffs filed a criminal case and Banamali was convicted in the said case. Presently, the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1-3 and others have been in possession of the suit pond jointly as owners thereof. The defendants with false statements filed Miscellaneous Case No. 19 of 1993-1994 against mutation of the suit property in the names of the plaintiffs. Upon hearing, mutation of the suit property in the names of the plaintiffs was cancelled. However, the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Brahmanbaria observed that the 2nd schedule i.e. the suit property and the suit pond are in possession of the plaintiffs. The defendant Nos. 13 were never owners or possessors of the 2nd schedule property i.e. the suit property. Recently, after cancellation of the names of the plaintiffs in the mutation case, the defendants are claiming that they are the owners of the suit property. In the above backdrop, the plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration of their title to the above properties by adverse possession.</u>

3. Defendant Nos. 1-3 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the averments made in the plaint of the suit contending, inter alia, that the suit property was duly recorded in the names of C.S. recorded owners and thereafter by amicable partition among the C.S. recorded owners Kunja and Sarupa got 58 decimals of land out of C.S. Plot Nos. 1069, 1068, 1064, 1060, 1063 and 1052 in their shares along with a share in the suit pond.

4. C.S. recorded tenant Mohan Nath while owner of C.S. Plot Nos. 1068 and 1064 measuring an area of 14 ½ decimals of land, died leaving behind 2(two) sons, namely, Puma Chand Debnath (Puma) and Banamali. The said sons became 8 annas owner each of the said property. While Kunja and Sarupa were in ejmali possession of 58 decimals of property, Sarupa died leaving behind Kunja as her sole heir. Kunja while owner of 29 decimals of land out of 58 decimals of land, gifted 29 decimals of land out of the said land to his wife Muktakeshi and grandsons Puma and Radhika. Radhika gifted his share to his wife Chapala. Chapala transferred the said land to Kali Mohan. Kunja while owner of the rest 29 decimals of land out of 58 decimals of land, died leaving behind wife Muktakeshi and daughter Suchitra as his heirs. Muktakeshi while owner of 29 decimals of land with Suchitra by inheritence and 9 2/3 decimals of land by way of gift from her husband, died leaving behind Suchitra as her sole heir. Suchitra became the owner of 38 2/3  decimals of land out of the said property and she due to legal necessity sold the said land to Banamali by a registered deed dated 24.02.1944 and delivered possession to him. Subsequently, the said deed was corrected as a plot number was wrongly recorded in the previous deed. But the said corrected deed was subsequently lost. Piyare while owner of 14 V2 decimals of land died leaving behind his son Puma and Banamali. They became the owners of the said land and also became the owner of 9 2/3 decimals of land from Kunja. Puma died unmarried leaving Banmali as his sole heir and Banamali became owner of total 62 2/3 decimals of land by way of inheritance and purchase and he had been in uninterrupted possession of the said land including the suit property and suit pond peacefully by exercising his own right for more than 12(twelve) years and his name was correctly recorded in the S.A. khatian. Mahananda, father of the plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 and their mother Indumoyee became shelterless after death of their father and they being relatives of Banamali, he permitted them to live in 08 decimals of land on the suit property and he was in possession of the rest 07 decimals of land out of it. Defendant Nos. 1-3 are now in possession of rest 07 decimals of land and also owner of 08 decimals of land. The plaintiffs were ejectable licensee of the defendants since the lifetime of their father but they collusively mutated their names relating to the suit property. Therefore, the defendants filed the miscellaneous case and the names of the plaintiffs were cancelled from the record-of-rights. Muktakeshi never filed any suit for partition against Banamali and Mahananda was not defendant No. 4 in the suit. Muktakeshi did not get 15 decimals of land of C.S. Plot No.1069 (suit property) and 109 decimals of land of C.S. Plot No. 1068 (suit pond). Muktakeshi neither sold the suit property to Sanatan by any registered deed nor he was in possession of the suit property at any time. The statements made in the plaint are all false and defendant Nos.1-3 are in possession of the suit property. The suit is liable to be dismissed.

Issues

5. The following issues were framed by the trial Court for deciding the suit:

“বিচার্য বিষয় সমূহঃ

১। বর্তমান আকারে ও প্রকারে অত্র মোকদ্দমা রক্ষণীয় কি না?

২। উপর্যুক্ত তায়দাদ ও কোর্ট ফি যুক্তি অত্র মোকদ্দমা দায়ের হইয়াছে কি না?

৩। নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে বাদীপক্ষের বিরুদ্ধে স্বত্ত্ব (Adverse possession) অর্জিত হইয়াছে কি না?

৪। বাদীপক্ষ তাহাদের প্রার্থীত মতে নালিশী দ্বিতীয় তপছিলের ভূমিতে ৪০ বৎসরের একক দখল এবং তৃতীয় তপছিলের পুকুরে এজমালিতে দখল আছে কি না?

৫। বাদী পক্ষ প্রার্থীত ডিক্রী পাইতে পারেন কি না?

Decision of the Trial Court

6. The trial Court, upon hearing the parties and in consideration of evidence on record by judgment and decree dated 30.10.1997, decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs and declared the plaintiffs' title to 15 decimals of land in 3/4. S. Plot No. 1069 (suit property) and 5 ¾ decimals share in the suit pond.

Decision of the Appellate Court (Title Appeal No. 118 of 1997)

7. Feeling aggrieved, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 118 of 1997 before the Court of District Judge, Brahmanbaria. Eventually, the appeal was heard by the 2na Court of Additional District Judge, Brahmanbaria (the Appellate Court) and the appeal was allowed in part by the judgment and decree dated 26.04.2006 and the Appellate Court modified the judgment and decree of the trial Court and declared the plaintiffs' title to 08 decimals of land in C.S. Plot No. 1069 only.

Revision before the High Court Division and result (Civil Revision No. 2359 of 2006)

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the plaintiffs moved the High Court Division by filing Civil Revision No. 2359 of 2006. The High Court Division, upon hearing, by judgment and decree dated 20.03.2012 made the Rule absolute and set aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court and restored those of the trial Court.

Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 303 of 2013

9. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division, the contesting defendants as leave petitioners, filed the aforesaid civil petition and leave was granted to consider the following grounds: "I. Because in passing the impugned judgment and order, the High Court Division completely disregarded the admission of P.W.1, Gangacharan made in his cross-examination to the effect that the defendants are in possession over 7 decimals of land of the 2na schedule property and, as such, the impugned judgment and order is outcome of total non-application of judicial mind and therefore, the same is liable to be set aside.

II. Because both the trial Court and the High Court Division in arriving at their findings as to possession of the plaintiffs relied upon exhibit-6 series which are tax receipts issued from

office of Brahmanbaria Pourashava and exhibit-7 which is a rent receipt but while relying on those documents both the Courts failed to notice that no plot number has been mentioned in the said Pourashava tax receipts and those are only for the years 1991 to 1995 and rent is only for the year 1399 B.S. corresponding to 1992 A.D. and, as such, came to an erroneous findings that the plaintiffs proved their title by adverse possession and therefore, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside."

10. This appeal is the outcome of the aforesaid civil petition.

Arguments of the appellant’s side

11. Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the appellants, has taken us through the various judgments and decrees passed by the trial Court, the Appellate Court, the High Court Division, the connected materials on record and put forward the following arguments before us:

1. The plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration of their title to the suit property and suit pond by way of adverse possession for more than 30/35 years. But the owners of the plots against whom the plaintiffs claim title to those properties by adverse possession were not made parties to the suit and therefore, the suit was not at all maintainable.

2. P.W.1 Gangacharan in his cross-examination admits that defendant Nos. 1-3 are in possession in 07 decimals of land out of the suit property and, as such, the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is without application of judicial mind and thus, the same is liable to be set aside.

3. Both the trial Court and the High Court Division though mainly decided the suit and revision considering Pourashava tax receipts issued from office of Brahmanbaria Pourashava (exhibit-6 series) and the rent receipt (exhibit-7), but both the Courts failed to notice that plot numbers were not mentioned in the said Pourashava tax receipts and those are only for the years 1991 to 1995 and the rent receipt is only for the year 1399 B.S. and the mutation in the names of the plaintiffs in the record-of-rights has been cancelled. The trial Court and the High Court Division without considering the value of those documents and the evidence on record erroneously decided that the plaintiffs proved their title to the suit property and the suit pond by way of adverse possession.

4. The decision of the Appellate Court relating to ownership and possession of defendant Nos. 1-3 relating to 07 decimals of land was correct as plaintiff No. 1 himself admitted it in his cross-examination. But the trial Court and the High Court Division without properly considering the evidence on record unlawfully decided that the plaintiffs are the owners of the entire suit property (2na schedule).

5. It is admitted in the plaint that both the plaintiffs and the defendants are in joint possession of the suit pond.

Therefore, the suit for declaration of title on the basis of the adverse possession in the suit pond where admittedly other co-sharers are in joint possession is not at all maintainable. Thus, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside and those of the Appellate Court is liable to be restored.

12. Mr. Alam, in support of his submissions has relied on the decisions of the following cases: (i) Pushpa Rani Saha Podder Vs. Rash Mohan Saha being dead his heirs:- Kartick Chowdhury Saha and others reported in 10 MLR (AD) 345; (ii) Md. Sheikh Farid and others Vs. Abdul Wadud Sikder and others reported in 12 MLR (AD) 201; (iii) Md. Ali Bepary and others Vs, Garupranjan Chakraborty and others reported in 14 BLC (AD) 97; (iv) Md. Abdul Rahman Vs. Abdul Jabbar and others reported in 13 DLR (HCD) 576; (v) Mt. Jahan Ara Begum Vs. A.L.Md. Shamsul Hoque reported in 27 DLR (AD) 129; and (vi) Probir Kumar Rakshit Vs. Abdas Sabur and others reported in 14 BLC (AD) 28.

Arguments of the respondents side

13. In reply, Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr. Subrata Saha, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondents, takes us through the judgment and decree of various Courts and the evidence on record and contends as under:

a) The plaintiffs by examining as many as 7(seven) witnesses proved their adverse possession in the suit property and the suit pond since the period of their predecessors in interest for more than 30/35 years.

b) The defendants failed to prove that they are in possession of the suit property for more than 12 (twelve) years. Rather, the defendants' witnesses admit that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit property (homestead).

c) The report relating to cancellation of plaintiffs' mutation also shows that the plaintiffs were/are in possession of the suit property. However, mutation in their names was cancelled as notices were not duly served upon all the co-sharers at the time of mutation of their names in the record-of-rights.

d) The owners through whom the plaintiffs claim the suit property and suit pond were/are not opposing their title to or possession in the suit property or the suit pond. Rather, defendant Nos. 1-3 were/are only claiming their ownership, title to and possession in the suit property and the suit pond. Therefore, the original owners were not necessary parties to the suit and the suit was maintainable and the appeal is thus liable to be dismissed.

14. However, Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan could not give any satisfactory reply as to how a suit for declaration of title to the suit pond by way of adverse possession would be maintainable, as admittedly all the co-sharers including defendant Nos. 1-3 and the plaintiffs are in joint possession of the suit pond.

15. Mr. Bhuiyan, in support of his arguments relating to acquisition of plaintiffs' title to the suit property by way of adverse possession, has relied on the decisions in the cases of-(1) Abdus Sattar Vs. Abdul Rahman @ Abdur Rahman and others reported in 44 DLR (AD) 100; and (2) Mir Laik Ali Vs. Standard Vacuum Oil Company (ES.50) and Abdur Razzak reported in 16 DLR (SC) 287.

Examination of Records

16. We have examined the judgments and decrees of various Courts and the evidence on record.

<u>Deliberation of the Court</u>

<u>17. It is an admitted proposition that C.S. recorded owners of the suit property and the suit pond along with other properties were Kunja, Raj, Piyare and Sarupa. The plaintiffs claimed their title to the suit property by adverse possession for the last 30/35 years.</u>

<u>18. In support of their case, the plaintiffs filed Municipality tax receipts and a rent receipt (exhibit-6 series and exhibit-7 respectively). However, those receipts are not relating to payment of Municipal tax to the Municipality or rent to the Government continuously for the last 30-35 years. Municipal tax receipts are for a few years and the rent receipt is, only for one year and those receipts do not contain the plot numbers. So, it cannot be presumed that those were/are for the suit property or the suit pond. However, the plaintiffs' case is that Muktakeshi sold the suit property by the deed dated 07.05.1942 to Sanatan and the other side denied it. The plaintiffs' further case is that Gangacharan and Mahananda purchased the suit property and the share of the suit pond from Sanatan who had purchased the same from Muktakeshi. Anyway, the deed of purchase of Gangacharan and Mahananda could not be registered and the actual owners did not claim the suit property or the suit pond from Gangacharan and Mahananda or heirs of Mahananda. The plaintiffs claim the suit property and the suit pond by way of adverse possession through Gangacharan and Mahananda against defendant Nos. 1-3, who claimed ownership of the suit property and the suit pond. Therefore, it cannot be said that the suit is not maintain-able as only the persons claiming owner-ship have been made parties to the suit.</u>

19. The trial Court decreed the suit by way of adverse possession in favour of the plaintiffs holing that the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit property peacefully and uninterruptedly for the last 30/35 years. The trial Court also declared the plaintiffs' title to 53/4 decimals out of the suit pond in ejmali.

20. The Appellate Court, on the other hand, allowed the appeal in part and declared the plaintiffs' title to 08 decimals of land (part of suit property) of C.S. Plot No. 1069 only by way of adverse possession in consideration of the evidence on record.

21. The High Court Division set aside the judgment of the Appellate Court and restored those of the trial Court.

22. Since the decision of the Appellate Court and the High Court Division are different, we have to decide the merit of this appeal on the evidence laid down by the parties relating to possession.

23. The plaintiffs in support of their possession have examined 7(seven) witnesses.

24. P.W.1 Gangacharan Debnath described the details of the plaint case. P.W.1 stated that they are in possession of the suit property since 1952 from the time of purchase thereof by Gangacharan and Mahananda and that they got delivery of possession of the suit property in the year 1952 from Sanatan. However, he could not remember the exact date. He also stated that although a deed was executed between Sanatan and Gangacharan as well as Mahananda it was not registered. It appears that he supported his case during the cross-examination stating as under:

“মুক্তকেশী কর্তৃক ০৭-০৫-৪২ ইং তারিখের সনাতন বরাবরে দলিলটি আদালতে দাখিল করি নাই। মুক্তকেশী যখন সনাতনের নিকট বিক্রয় করে তখন আমি উপস্থিত ছিলাম এবং ১৯৪৪ সনে উক্ত খরিদ বিক্রি হয় এবং তখন নিত্যানন্দ পাল (মনত), স্বীয় লক্ষী কান্ত দেবনাথ, উপেন্দ্র দেবনাথ (মৃত), এরা তখন উপস্থিত ছিল। উক্ত ব্যক্তিদের কেহ জীবিত নাই এবং উক্ত লেন-দেনের ব্যক্তিগন জীবিত নাই। বিক্রির পরে পুকুরে মুক্তকেশীর তিন আনা অংশ ছিল। মুক্তকেশী নাঃ পুকুরের অংশ ইন্দমোহন ও গোপিনাথ সাহা বরাবর ২ পয়সার অংশ, পরেশ

দেবনাথ বরাবর এক পয়সা, নারায়ন খান বরাবর ১ পয়সা, সুরেন্দ্র নাথ বরাবর ২ পয়সা, অমর পাল বরাবর ২ পয়সা, লক্ষীকান্ত দেবনাথ বরাবর এক আনা অংশ বিক্রি করিয়াছে। আমি উক্ত বিক্রয় দলিলে সাক্ষী ছিলাম না। মুক্তকেশী আমার সহিত পরামর্শ করিয়া উক্ত বিক্রয় করে নাই এবং আমি তাহাতে উপস্থিত ছিলাম না। সত্য নহে যে মুক্তকেশী কোন জায়গা সনাতন বরাবর বিক্রয় করে নাই। মাইঝ পাড়া গ্রামে সনাতন নামে কোন লোক ছিল না ইহা সত্য নহে। বনমালী দেবনাথ (১-৩ নং বিবাদীর পিতা) নামে দলিলের সময় উপস্থিতে ছিলাম না। বনমালী নামে দলিল আমার কাছে আছে। বনমালী সুচিত্রা দেবনাথ হইতে খরিদ করিয়াছে। সূচিত্রা ও বনমালীর মধ্যে বেচাকেনা, কথাবার্তার সময় ছিলাম না। সনাতনের ওয়ারিশ কে আছে বলিতে পারি না । সনাতন আমার বরাবর আনরেজিষ্ট্রি দলিল দিয়েছিল এবং উক্ত দলিলটি পুড়িয়া গিয়াছে। উক্ত দলিল পুড়িবার বিষয়ে আমার উকিল সাহেবকে বলিয়াছি। সত্য নয় যে, বনমালি মৃত্যুবরণ করিলে ১-৩ নং বিবাদী তাহার ওয়ারিশ হিসাবে নাঃ ভূমিতে মালিক দখলকার আছে। সত্য নহে যে, বনমালির মৃত্যুর পর বনমালির পুত্র উত্তরকারী বিবাদীগণের নিকট হইতে অনুমতি লইয়া আমরা দখলকার আছি ১০৬৯ দাগে ৮ শতকে। সত্য নয় যে, বেআইনীভাবে খারিজা খতিয়ান করিলে তাহা বাতিল হইয়াছে। সত্য নয় যে, নাঃ জমি হইতে চলিয়া যাইতে উত্তরকারী বিবাদীগণ তলব তাগাদা করিয়াছে। সত্য নয় যে, আমরা নাঃ জমি হইতে চলিয়া যাইতে আইনতঃ বাধ্য। ১০৬৯ দাগে ৭ শতক ভূমি উত্তরকারী বিবাদি দখলকার আছে। সত্য নহে যে, উত্তরকারী বিবাদি গণ বক্রি ভূমিতে সবজি করিয়া ও পুকুরে মাছ চাষ করিয়া দখলকার আছে।

১০৬৮ দাগের পুকুরে আমাদের দখল নাই ইহা সত্য নহে। ১০৬৮ দাগের পুকুর বাবদ দখলের কাগজ দাখিল করি নাই।”

25. It appears that the Appellate Court decided that plaintiff No. 1 Gangacharan himself admitted possession of contested defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 by deposing “১০৬৯ দাগে ৭ শতক ভূমি উত্তরকারী বিবাদী দখলকার আছে” But from his statement as a whole, quoted hereinbefore, it appears that in the next sentence, he denied “সত্য নহে যে, উত্তরকারী বিবাদীগণ বক্রি ভূমিতে সবজী করিয়া ও পুকুরে মাছ চাষ করিয়া দখলকার আছে”.

26. Moreover, from the deposition of P.W.1 as a whole, it is evident that in fact, P.W.1 denied that the possession of defendant Nos. 1-3 in 07 decimals of land or in any part of the suit property. But due to a "।" (দাঁড়ি) between the words, the Appellate Court decided that plaintiff No. 1 (P.W.1) admitted the possession of the defendant Nos. 1-3, which is not the correct picture. Moreover, P.W.2 Manmohan Majumder stated that he constructed his house in 1973 near the suit property. Since then he has seen the plaintiffs in possession of the suit property. This witness is an old man of 80 years. P.W.3 Poresh Chandra Debnath aged 45 years stated that he has been seeing the plaintiffs in possession of the suit property since his childhood. P.W.5 Kazi Abdul Bari stated that in 1969 he started living near the suit property. Since then be has seen the plaintiffs in possession of the suit property. P.W.4 Baikontha Debnath, P.W. 6 Radha Charan Debnath and P.W.7 Surendra Chandra Paul all in a voice sup-ported possession of the plaintiffs in the suit property for the last 30-35 years. Some from the years 1969, 1971 and 1973, when they started living near the suit property i.e. more than 20 years back. It also appears that P.W.4 Baikontha Debnath deposed that the plaintiffs' house is at the north side of the suit pond and the defendant Nos. 1-3's house is at the south side of the suit pond. D.W.1 Binod Biheri Debnath in his cross-examination also admitted that “নালিশী পুকুরের লাগ দক্ষিণে আমাদের বসত ঘর। নালিশী পুকুরের লাগ উত্তরে বাদীদের বসত বাড়ী”।

27. Now let us examine how far the contesting defendants have been able to prove their case of possession in the suit property.

28. D.W.1 in his examination-in-chief supports the defendants' case. During cross-examination, he initially denied that Muktakeshi filed a suit against his father Banamali and Raj being Partition Suit No. 241 of 1939 but then stated that suit was collusive and that he has no knowledge about the suit. He claims that the plain-tiffs' father was in permissive possession of 08 decimals of land from the suit property but could not say if there was any agreement between Mahananda Debnath, plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3's father and the defendant Nos. 1-3's father. He admitted that the defendants never issued any notice for their eviction at any time. He also admits neither their father nor they ever paid Municipal/Pourashava taxes of the suit property. He also admits that the deed through which his father allegedly claimed the suit property from Suchitra was destroyed in 1971. He also admits that presently a homestead is situated in the suit property. He further admits that their house is situated towards the contiguous south of the suit pond and the house of the plaintiffs is towards the north side of the suit pond. He further admits that there is a road after the suit pond and then the suit property. He further admitted property. He further admitted “নালিশা পুকুরের লাগ দক্ষিণে আমাদের বসত ঘর। নালিশী পুকরের লাগ উত্তরে বাদীদের নালিশী বাড়ী। পুকুরটি ১৬০-১৬৫ হাত লম্বা হইবে । নালিশী পুকুরের সংলগ্ন উত্তরে পৌরসভার রাস্তা তৎপর নালিশী বাড়ী। নালিশী বাড়ীর উত্তর/দক্ষিণ্/পূর্ব/ পশ্চিম ভিটিতে ঘর আছে। বাড়ীতে পাকা ল্যাট্রিন ও টিউব-ওয়েল আছে। নালিশী ভূমি একটি Compact এবং চারিদিকে ওয়াল এবং তাহাতে বাহির হইবার জন্য বেড়ার গেট আছে ।”Thus, from the statement of D.W.1, it is clear that the suit property is a house with boundary walls. Therefore, it is hardly believable that those defendants are in possession in part of the suit property by cultivating vegetables.

29. D.W.2 Abdul Kadir claims that his Uncle Bashu Miah used to cultivate the suit property by taking 'Barga' and that the plaintiffs are in possession of half of the suit property and the rest are in the possession of the defendants. During cross-examination, he could not say the name of the father of the plaintiffs. He also admits that the suit house is surrounded with Bera (বেড়া) in three side and there are four houses in four side of the suit property. Thus, it appears that he could not prove possession of the defendants in any part of the suit property.

30. D.W.3 Dhan Miah though mentioned that he was a 'Bargader' in the suit property under Banamali relating to half of the suit property, but during cross-examination, he admits that “নালিশী বাড়ীর ৪ ভিটিতে ৪টি ঘর আছে” So it appears from his statement, there are four houses in four side of the suit property, which is also the case of the plaintiffs.

31. D.W.4 Md. Mostaque Ahmed stated that the deed of purchase of Banamali and Suchitra as shown in the certified copy tallied with the volume. The deed of correction also tallied with the volume. So, it appears that he is an official witness only.

32. It appears from the evidence on record as discussed that the plaintiffs though could not produce the document of purchase of the suit property from Mulctakeshi by Sanatan or purchase of the suit property by Gangacharan and Mahananda from Sanatan, but they could prove their exclusive uninterrupted possession in the suit property by erecting four houses and living there for more than 30/35 years. On the other hand, the defendants' witnesses could not prove their possession. Rather, one of the defendants, D.W.1 admits that the suit property is a compact property with boundaries in four side of the land.

33. In consideration of the evidence on record, we are of the view that both the trial Court as well as the High Court Division properly decided that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit property uninterruptedly for more than 30-35 years.

We find no misreading or non-consideration of the evidence on record by the trial Court or the High Court Division. Therefore, the declaration of the plaintiffs' title to the suit property (C.S. Plot No. 1069, 2nd schedule property) appears to be lawful. It appears that the Appellate Court considering only a part of the statement made by P. W.1 during the cross-examination decided that the plaintiffs admitted possession of the defendants relating to 07 decimals of land without considering the whole statement of the P. W.1 erroneously.

34. However, so far the suit pond is concerned, it appears that in the plaint of suit, the plaintiffs claimed adverse possession in the suit pond relating to some shares. It also appears that the defendant Nos. 1-3 also enjoy the suit pond as co-sharers along with other co-sharers jointly. From the deposition of witnesses it is also found that the plaintiffs, the defendants and other co-sharers enjoy the suit pond jointly. Therefore, the decision of the trial Court as well as the High Court Division declaring 53/4 decimals share of the suit pond to the plaintiffs by adverse possession is not tenable. The plaintiffs, the defendants and others are in ejmali (joint) possession of the suit pond. Ejmali possession of co-sharers in the suit pond means all of them are in joint possession of every inch of the suit pond. Thus, declaration of the plaintiffs' title to certain share of the suit pond by adverse possession by the trial Court and the High Court Division appears to be ,erroneous and liable to be interfered with.

35. We have considered the decisions as referred to by the learned Senior Advocates for the contending parties. We find that the decisions as referred to by Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam are not applicable in the instant case as the facts and circumstances of the present case is distinguishable with the facts and circumstances of the referred cases. Similarly, the decisions as referred to by Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan are not also applicable in this case as the facts of the referred cases are quite distinguishable from the instant case.

36. In view of the discussions made hereinbefore, we find part merit in the appeal.

37. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part without any order as to costs.

<u>38. The judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and the High, Court Division, so far as it relates to 3rd schedule property (suit pond) is hereby set aside and those of the Appellate Court i§ restored i.e. the suit relating to the 3rd schedule property is dismissed. The judgment and decree in favour of the plaintiffs relating to the suit property (2nd schedule) is hereby affirmed.</u>
